content.text:
I read the code for all three and tested your running MLX server. The first gap was described wrongly last session, the second has no principled reason behind it, and the third is real.

## 1. MLX and the reasoning setting

Your server does turn thinking off, so "the MLX server ignores the setting" was inaccurate. What actually happens:

- **The Rust client drops the setting.** `src/mlx/client.rs:105` takes `_reasoning` and sends `reasoning: None`.
- **The server has no such field.** `ChatCompletionRequest` in `mlx-server/schemas.py:67` only has model, messages, `max_tokens` and temperature.
- **The server turns thinking off itself, on every request.** `mlx-server/server.py:402` and `:437` pass `enable_thinking=False` to the chat template.

For your configured model this works. The `Qwen3.5-0.8B-OptiQ-4bit` template reads the flag and pre-fills an empty `<think></think>` block. I sent one test chat to `localhost:8678` with `max_tokens: 32`, and it answered in 3 tokens with `finish_reason: stop`.

The real gap is narrower:

- **The flag is only a template variable.** A model whose chat template never reads `enable_thinking` will think anyway, with no error. I could not check your commented-out `gemma-4-e4b-it-mxfp4`, because it is not in the local cache.
- **There is no fallback for that case.** The OpenRouter path retries with 2,048 extra tokens when a model refuses to stop reasoning (`src/app/dispatch.rs:882`). The MLX path has nothing equivalent.
- **The error would be misleading.** `server.py:419` counts completion tokens after stripping the thinking text. A model that spent its whole budget thinking reports `stop` with empty content, not `length`.

## 2. Why Jev is retried and chat is not

There is no design reason; the retry was added where failures were seen. HuggingFace is not a chat provider here: `src/huggingface/` only searches the Hub for models, so chat means MLX or OpenRouter.

- **Jev failed in live tests.** Commits `946366f` and `4e6944a` added the retry after a dropped connection hit one of three requests and left a cluster unlabelled.
- **Jev fans out.** `:topics` sends one Jev request per cluster, up to 8 at once, so rate limits and drops are much more likely than for the single chat request.
- **Chat already has a fallback when Jev is on.** A failed chat request falls back to the Jev taxonomy (`dispatch.rs:366`–`393`). Without `[jev]`, a chat failure goes straight to an error popup.
- **Neither chat client retries anything.** `OpenRouterClient::post` and `MlxClient` send once and set no timeout. This also covers embeddings.

Adding a retry to chat is reasonable, with two cautions:

- **OpenRouter:** a drop after generation means paying for the tokens twice.
- **MLX:** the server keeps generating after the client disconnects, on a single MLX thread. A retry queues behind the abandoned run.

I would retry connect and send errors plus 429/5xx, once or twice, in one helper shared by both clients.

## 3. Can the hint differ from what runs?

Yes. The hint comes from `topic_labeller_name()` (`dispatch.rs:617`), which looks only at config and is re-read on every frame (`src/ui/cluster.rs:266`). The route is decided later inside the spawned task.

With your config (`[jev]` with `propose_labels` on by default, plus MLX chat) the hint always says "MLX + Jev". What actually runs can be:

| What happens | Actual labeller |
|---|---|
| At least half the posts are in tech clusters and the proposal covers every cluster | MLX + Jev |
| Fewer than half are tech, or the tech check fails | MLX alone |
| The proposal misses a cluster, or the chat request fails or returns partial labels | Jev taxonomy |

The final status message is correct, because it uses the labeller name the task sends back (`event_handlers.rs:499`). Only the in-progress hint is wrong. The fix is for the task to report its stage as it goes.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- `enable_thinking` is not a model or server feature. It is a variable that a Jinja chat template may or may not read, and Jinja silently ignores variables it does not use. That is why "off" can fail without any error.
- The hint is derived from config while the route is decided at run time from Jev's answers. A value computed in two places can drift; having the task report its own stage removes the second source.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

I changed nothing in the repo. If you want these fixed, I'd take them in this order: the hint (small), the chat retry, then MLX budget headroom with a correct `finish_reason`.

Both are done in the working tree, uncommitted, with no chat retries for dropped connections. Restart the server on port 8678 to pick up the budget change; it is still running the old code.

## Loading hint

The hint now shows the labeller that is actually running, not the one the config predicts.

- **How it works:** the `:topics` task sends a new `ClusterTopicsLabeller` event each time it starts a step that writes labels. The cluster list title reads that value.
- **What you see:** `generating labels...` during Jev's tech check, then `generating labels via MLX + Jev...` or `via MLX...`. If the request falls back to the taxonomy, it changes to `via Jev...`.
- **Removed:** `topic_labeller_name()`, the config-based guess.

## MLX budget headroom

Gemma is fine as configured: its chat template honours the thinking switch, and it answered the label prompt in 25 tokens on your running server. The fix covers models that think anyway.

- **Server reports what was generated.** `mlx-server/server.py` now returns the real generated-token count, the backend's own `finish_reason`, and `usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens`. Before, a reply that was all thinking came back as `stop` with empty content.
- **Client asks once more with room.** When an MLX reply is cut off and has reasoning tokens, `complete_text` in `src/app/dispatch.rs` repeats the request with 2,048 extra tokens, the same headroom the OpenRouter path uses. A reply cut off without reasoning is kept, since more room would not help.
- **Clearer error.** If the model is still thinking after the headroom, the popup says the budget was exhausted on reasoning.
- **One bug found on the way.** Some templates open the `<think>` block in the prompt, so the output only carries the closing tag. The server did not strip that, and the thinking leaked into the labels. It does now.

I forced thinking on with your two real models to check the accounting:

| Model | 48-token budget | With headroom |
|---|---|---|
| Gemma 4 e4b | cut off, empty answer | finished in 462 tokens, 27 of them the answer |
| Qwen3.5 0.8B | cut off, empty answer | still thinking at 2,096 tokens |

So headroom rescues a model that thinks briefly, not one that never stops. That case now gets the clear error.

## Verification

- **Rust:** 108 tests pass; `cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy` are clean. New tests cover the headroom retry against a local stand-in server, and the hint state.
- **Server:** 46 pytest tests pass and ruff is clean. `ty` reports 3 findings, all in `image_security.py`, which I did not touch.
- **Live:** the modified server answered real requests on a spare port with the new usage fields.
- **Not run:** the hint through a real Jev request. The Jev URL is a constant, so only the chat-only route is tested end to end.

I also updated `README.md`, `docs/jev-design.md` and `mlx-server/AGENTS.md`.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- The server computed `finish_reason` from the text left after stripping. Deriving a status from cleaned output hides the very failure the status exists to report.
- `reasoning_tokens` under `completion_tokens_details` is the standard OpenAI usage field, so the client check is a single test that works for any provider reporting it.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

The retry rule is `reasoning_exhausted_budget()` in `src/openrouter/types.rs`: cut off and any reasoning tokens. Say if you want it stricter, for example only when the answer is empty.

Here is a note offered by a side agent:

> Heads up · The MLX budget fix is being built as a second request with a bigger budget, even though you said no chat retries.
>
> **MLX headroom works by asking twice**
> You said chat needs no retries. The main agent read that as "no retries for dropped connections" and is still planning one kind of repeat for MLX:
> * If a local model spends its token budget on thinking and the answer is cut off, the app sends the same request again with 2,048 extra tokens.
> * The first run is thrown away, so `:topics` takes longer on such a model.
> * Both of your models (Gemma and the small Qwen) switch thinking off correctly, so this should not trigger for you today.
> * In a forced test, the small Qwen still never finished thinking with the extra room.
> The alternative is letting the server give thinking extra room in one run. **Say so in the main session if you prefer that.**

The PR had one review comment, from Codex, and it is fixed, answered and resolved on [PR #94](https://github.com/jessearmand/xplorertui/pull/94). CI on the new commit was still running when I checked; `fmt` and GitGuardian had passed and the rest were pending.

## The comment

When the server stopped a reply at the answer cap, it closed the model's token stream early. The stream's detokenizer can hold back the text of the newest tokens until a later token arrives, so that text was lost even though its tokens were counted.

The reviewer was right, and I reproduced it on a real model: through `mlx-vlm`, Gemma with a 6-token cap returned "Cluster 0: Rust" when the tokens spelled "Cluster 0: Rust programming".

## The fix

- **What changed:** when the server stops a reply itself, it now rebuilds the text from the generated tokens with a fresh detokenizer of the same kind the stream uses. A reply that ends on its own is handled as before.
- **Why not finalize the stream's own detokenizer:** neither library exposes it. `mlx-lm` hands out a new instance on each access, and `mlx-vlm` makes a private copy.
- **Tests:** the test stream now behaves like the real `mlx-lm` one, and three new tests cover held-back text at the cap, with and without thinking. 49 server tests pass; ruff is clean.
- **Real models:** the 6-token Gemma case now returns "Cluster 0: Rust programming" through both backends, and the forced-thinking runs still return complete labels in one run.

The commit is `1f515e7` in `mlx-server/server.py` and `mlx-server/test_chat_usage.py`. No Rust code changed.

## Server

I restarted the server on port 8678 with this fix; it returns the full 6-token text over HTTP. It still runs as a background task of this session, logging to `scratchpad/mlx-server.log`.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- Streamed text and generated tokens are not the same sequence. A streaming detokenizer emits text only when it is sure of it, so stopping a stream by closing it can drop the last word.
- My first test stream sent each token's text immediately, so it could not show this bug. Making the fake mirror the real stream's shape is what let the tests catch it.
